clue.text: Clear statement of principles, missing nothing

indicators.note: missing tells us a letter is dropped from the document named by the following words

parts.note: a manifesto is a published statement of principles
O, shaped like a zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A party document set out plainly, with nothing left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear statement of principles' reads as one phrase, but 'Clear' alone is the definition; dropping O (nothing) from MANIFESTO leaves the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something manifest is obvious and plain to see, a synonym for clear.

clue.text: I'm playful — and the month hasn't even started!

indicators.note: a word that has not started has lost its opening letter, so the month's first letter goes

parts.note: March is a month of the year

explanation.surface: Someone feeling mischievous before the calendar has even turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue speaks in the first person: 'I'm playful' is the answer describing itself. MARCH without its first letter M gives the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch describes a knowing, teasing, mischievous manner, a synonym for playful.

clue.text: One's game is clumsy — it stops one carrying on, perhaps

definitions.text: it stops one carrying on, perhaps

indicators.note: clumsy means awkwardly put together, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's play is awkward, which may keep them from continuing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clumsy' is the anagram signal on GAME IS; the definition is a cryptic description, since prejudice against age can force people out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrimination against older people may stop a person continuing in a job, hence the 'perhaps' marking an example.

clue.text: It's clever to eat vegetable with a smooth manner

indicators.note: to eat means to take something inside, so one word is put within another

parts.note: a leek is an onion-family vegetable

explanation.surface: A suave diner's polished way of tackling a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is 'to eat': the clever word swallows the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleekly means in a glossy, polished, suave way, which is acting with a smooth manner.

clue.text: I'm thought to have magical powers, able to unlock ATM with nails

definitions.text: I'm thought to have magical powers

indicators.note: unlock suggests prising something open and rearranging, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A burglar boasts of breaking into a cash machine with nails.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in the first person: the answer speaks of itself. 'unlock' scrambles ATM and NAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm or amulet believed to carry magic protective power is exactly what the word names.

clue.text: It's cheek to require money first, even for an essential part of Christmas dinner

definitions.text: an essential part of Christmas dinner

indicators.note: first says the money comes at the front, before the cheek

explanation.surface: A complaint about being asked to pay upfront even for festive dinner essentials.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'first' puts the money ahead of the cheek. Bread sauce, a milk sauce thickened with breadcrumbs, is traditionally served with the British Christmas turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread sauce is the traditional British accompaniment to roast turkey, a staple of the Christmas meal.

clue.text: A process of voting on love god

parts.note: a poll is a vote or ballot
love means nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A ballot about the deity of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love god' looks like one phrase meaning Cupid or Eros, but 'love' gives O and 'god' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo is the Greek and Roman deity of the sun, music and poetry.

clue.text: Unaccompanied song disturbed girl with Adam

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A song without instruments upset a girl who was with Adam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' is the anagram signal over GIRL and ADAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a part song for several voices, usually sung without instruments.

clue.text: It's unexpected for a brother to get up on time

explanation.surface: A sibling getting out of bed promptly is a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up on time' suggests punctuality, but each word is simply a piece in the chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrupt means sudden and without warning, which is a close synonym of unexpected.

clue.text: Knockout gets Sid back to hospital

indicators.note: back says the name Sid is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A man named Sid is knocked out and taken back to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'back' turns the name round; 'Knockout' is a stunner, not a boxing result.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is informal for a very attractive person, which is what a knockout also means.

clue.text: Having got in, I've turned to get food — that's certain

indicators.note: turned says the letters of I've are read backwards

parts.note: the letters of I've without the apostrophe
table can mean the food served, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: Once someone arrives, they will surely head for the food.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'turned' reverses I've (apostrophe ignored). Food is the fare served, as in 'keeps a good table'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inevitable means bound to happen, so something certain to occur.

clue.text: Light almost behind bed causes confusion

indicators.note: behind says the trimmed light comes after the bed
almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A bedside light knocked down causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicators are 'almost', which trims the light, and 'behind', which sets it after the bed. Bedlam was a London asylum, hence its use for uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam means a scene of uproar and chaos, a synonym for confusion.

clue.text: A warmer athlete?

parts.note: read as a garment, a long woollen sweater keeps you warm; read as a person, it is a competitor in a field event

explanation.walkthrough: In British English a jumper is a knitted sweater, so a long one is a warmer; the same two words name an athlete in a field event.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both an athlete in the jumping event and, loosely, a lengthy woollen sweater.

clue.text: In Cyprus you'll find Miss Lola, debauched

indicators.note: debauched means corrupted or led astray, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman named Lola is found behaving wildly on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'debauched' scrambles MISS LOLA; the definition is a place that you'll find in Cyprus.
explanation.definitionFit: Limassol is a port city on the south coast of the island, so a place located there.

clue.text: Patterned plate for various clients

indicators.note: various suggests differing forms, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A decorated plate made for assorted customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges CLIENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut sheet used to transfer a pattern, a patterned plate.

clue.text: It's impertinent to get in so fast

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: It is rude to push into a queue so quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' reads as quick but is the noun: a period of abstinence, Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent means rudely disrespectful, a direct synonym of impertinent.

clue.text: Very cruel to make a bee sound first in the bar

indicators.note: in places the bee noise and the article inside the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub or bar

indicators.note: first says the bee noise goes ahead of the article

explanation.surface: A heartless prank, buzzing like a bee in the pub first thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicators: 'first' sets the bee noise ahead of the article, and 'in' places both inside the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhuman describes brutality lacking all compassion, extreme cruelty.

clue.text: Sailor's discourse is theoretical

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor; the 's adds S
a tract is a written treatise or discourse

explanation.surface: A seaman's lecture is all about ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: AB is an able-bodied seaman; the 's of 'Sailor's' supplies the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstract means existing in thought rather than in concrete reality, which is theoretical.

clue.text: It's able to become savage

indicators.note: to become signals a transformation, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of it's without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Something that can turn wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' rearranges ITS and ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bestial means beast-like and brutal, a synonym of savage.

clue.text: The right word's unspoken in this country

definitions.text: The right word's unspoken in this country

parts.words: The right word's unspoken in this country
parts.note: the French phrase for the exactly apt term is French, not English, so in Britain the right word is not in the native tongue

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means 'the exactly right word' but is French, so in Britain it is a foreign expression rather than a native one.
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing means the precisely appropriate expression for something.

clue.text: Stupid old boy wants boiled suet

indicators.note: boiled suggests cooking and churning, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dim elderly lad wants his suet pudding cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'boiled' rearranges the suet, which follows the abbreviations for old and boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow to understand, dull-witted, a synonym of stupid.

clue.text: Animal guarding the Queen's front

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding protectively, so one word goes around another

parts.note: R, for Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A beast protects the monarch's front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guarding' puts R (Regina, the Queen) inside BEAST.
explanation.definitionFit: The breast is the front of the chest, so the front of a person or animal.

clue.text: Age and date of birth set up in this kind of shop

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means written upwards, so the letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone's age and birthday are recorded in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses AGEDOB to give BODEGA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a small grocery or wine shop, especially in Spain or Hispanic US neighbourhoods.

clue.text: Stirred by feelings, I must break with dead daughter

indicators.note: break means smash apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An emotional parting from a deceased daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges I MUST into STIMU, followed by LATE and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stimulated is to be roused or excited, emotionally stirred.

clue.text: Right to cut awful poet

indicators.note: to cut means to slice into, so one letter goes inside the word

explanation.surface: It is fair to criticise a dreadful versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' puts R into BAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A bard is a poet, especially one in the old minstrel tradition.

clue.text: Notice given to Mr Sikes

definitions.meaning: a printed poster or public announcement
the burglar Sikes in Dickens's Oliver Twist has this first name

explanation.surface: An announcement made to a gentleman named Sikes.
explanation.definitionFit: A posted notice is a poster; Dickens's villain Sikes in Oliver Twist has this first name.

clue.text: Like a bird's behind?

explanation.surface: A question about what a bird's rear looks like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like a bird' reads as AS TERN; 'behind' then becomes the nautical adverb, not a bird's rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is the nautical word for at or towards the back of a ship.

clue.text: Old painter, kind person, one in need of company

parts.note: an angel is a kind, helpful person
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An elderly artist, a gentle soul, lonely and in need of companions.
explanation.walkthrough: Fra Angelico was a fifteenth-century Florentine painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fra Angelico was an early Renaissance Italian artist, so a painter of long ago.
